title: The Milky Way over Paranal
caption: The Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The dark outline of the Very Large Telescope on top of Paranal Mountain stands out against a sky thick with stars. The sky here is so good that stars remain clearly visible right down to the horizon, above the clouds that usually cover the Pacific Ocean, only 12 km from the observatory.

The brightest area, crossed by strong dark lanes, is the central bulge of our galaxy, which we see edge-on. Rising through the galaxy's center is a brighter vertical column, the zodiacal light. It traces the plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun, the same plane in which the planets, the Sun, the Moon and the zodiacal constellations lie.
At the end of a dark lane that seems to hang down from the Galactic Center shines the bright star Antares, also known as Alpha Scorpii.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the zodiacal light and the Milky Way's dark lanes appear more strongly than they would to an observer.

explore: Zodiacal light is sunlight scattered by fine dust spread through the inner Solar System, which is why it follows the same path across the sky as the Sun and planets.
alt: The dark silhouette of telescope buildings on a mountain under a starry sky, with the bright Milky Way core crossed by dark lanes and a vertical column of faint light.
